attempts.summary: Created the appworker account on node1 (Alpine Linux 3.23) and configured its login sessions to a hard/soft limit of 8192 open files and 256 processes. Since node1's openssh-server build is not linked against PAM (confirmed via ldd) and its login is busybox (no PAM support either), /etc/security/limits.d alone would not be enforced. I implemented a working solution: (1) /etc/security/limits.d/appworker.conf documents the intended limits, (2) sshd's OpenRC conf.d (/etc/conf.d/sshd, rc_ulimit) raises the nofile hard ceiling to 8192 for sshd-spawned sessions, and (3) appworker's login shell was set to a small wrapper (/usr/local/sbin/appworker-shell) that applies `ulimit -n 8192; ulimit -u 256` before exec'ing ash, so both interactive and non-interactive SSH sessions are covered. Verified end-to-end via real SSH logins as appworker (using the cluster SSH keypair) both before and after a full native node restart, confirming soft=hard=8192 for nofile and soft=hard=256 for nproc in the actual login session. Completed the mandatory single-node restart-evidence protocol: captured boot_id baseline (59f3a348...) and service/config health, issued a background `reboot`, polled until the node reconnected, confirmed a changed boot_id (61ffa776...) with a fresh low uptime, and confirmed the appworker account, its limits configuration, wrapper shell, sshd service, and actual enforced session limits all recovered correctly.
